evidence: Verified frozen HEAD 3abee5a6add69443e49322e96f9130b834686235 against base 565def869ae50e47e6da7388ea333229050eaf8d. (a) Present under another name: no cancellation-aware owner acquisition exists. PresentationState::permit only chooses a shared Arc<Mutex<()>> and bounds its weak cache; src/service/delivery_presentation.rs:62 and :306 then call unconditional lock() before either budget-aware canonical view. ModChannelRegistry::presentation_owner delegates to that same cache (src/service/mod_channels.rs:696-698). DomainService::handle_with_output routes both commands directly to these methods (:1426-1429), with no FairWriter or other cancellation-aware gate serializing them first. Later store budget checks cannot execute while the caller is blocked in this acquisition. The library premise is grounded in fetched official Rust documentation, https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.Mutex.html#method.lock: 'This function will block the local thread until it is available to acquire the mutex.' The CallBudget token is separate from this mutex and is neither polled nor subscribed here. (b) Within contract: resume-watch-owner-replay-design.md:41 explicitly requires the owner fence before Live lease admission and through store/ledger/replay installation, but does not require or accept ignoring the waiting request's budget. Its budget-error rollback requirement (:100) and TRUST-POLICY.md:1714-1715 preserve cancellation and time budgets. StoreContext's accepted limit (src/store/connection.rs:330-336) concerns physical commit/fsync and an already accepted decision's independent storage outcome; the second caller has acquired no owner or decision, so that limit does not justify its uncancellable predecision wait. Source preserves that distinction in SqliteStore::presentation_pull (src/store/mod.rs:1303-1312); the existing writer contention loop checks the live budget before every try_lock and after acquisition (:355-385). (c) Scope: this is existing V2 Hook/Watch Pull and Confirm operation cancellation, not a demand to abort accepted commits, guarantee storage latency, increase throughput, or exceed bounded capacity. The bounded-successful-quantum and no-progress-under-perpetual-failure limits do not permit retaining an unrelated cancelled predecision caller. (d) Materiality: owner is held across store.presentation_pull (:199-216) through post-store replay installation (:282-288), including any slow commit. Another same-seat request can expire or disconnect while waiting, but transport.rs:514-533 only cancels its token and then awaits its synchronous worker before releasing admission. Each ordinary V2 RPC therefore retains a slot from the shared 32-slot pool (transport.rs:31, :192, :210-231, :319-320) for the first owner's remaining work, even after the five-second ordinary deadline. Repeated overlapping hooks or reconnect requests can occupy otherwise releasable slots and defer unrelated requests; no data-loss claim is needed for this availability regression. Existing owner tests prove the lock spans real paused store work (tests/service/delivery_pull.rs:13383-13465); the pre-cancelled replay test (:13087-13100) has no held owner and therefore does not cover this wait. Deterministically, hold the exact registry presentation_owner Arc, dispatch a valid Pull or Confirm with an already cancelled/expired budget on another thread, and it cannot return until that guard is released. This is a structural proof; no runtime experiment was performed or required. (e) Pre-existing: delivery_presentation.rs is absent on base. Base delivery_pull.rs:88-95 and :343-373 confines its ledger mutex to short in-memory snapshots outside store reads; base ModChannelRegistry has no presentation owner mutex. The transport's worker-drain rule and unbounded accepted commit time are inherited, but the new per-seat predecision wait materially introduces this amplification, so preExisting does not apply. (f) Linter territory: this is runtime cancellation/resource retention, not style. Severity Should-fix: significant bounded-admission availability risk; canonical mutation safety remains intact.
